newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills trade almost flat at open.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills trade almost flat at open.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened fairly steady on Friday but investors were poised to take the market lower if the Canadian currency eased.

"It's mostly dominated by currency fears," one money market trader said. The dollar opened firmer at C$1.3802 (US$0.7245) from C$1.3815 (US$0.7238) at the close of trading on Thursday but has slipped from last month's strength. "We're directionless during that instability," he added.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded to yield 3.35 percent from 3.36 percent at Thursday's close.

Another trader said that investors were concerned that the central bank may be tempted to raise short-term interest rates for the second time this year to prop up the currency. "There's continuing speculation when the Bank of Canada is going to come in and hike rates."
The first trader said: "It is causing yields to be a little higher than they should be," pushing domestic accounts to the sidelines.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill stayed steady at a yield of 3.73 percent from Thursday's close.
Stronger than expected U.S. durable goods orders for June had little impact, the second dealer said.
Orders rose 2.3 percent, their biggest jump since January and higher than the forecasted 1.4 percent rise.
The one-year when-issued T-bill was steady at a yield of 4.24 percent from Thursday's close.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
